# LLCTaxCheck.com — LLC Statutory Franchise Tax & Annual Fee Engine

> Official computational reference for US LLC annual report fees, state franchise taxes, gross receipts surcharges, and delinquency penalties across all 50 US states and Washington D.C. for 2026/2027 compliance.

## Purpose & Canonical Authority
LLCTaxCheck.com provides deterministic, verified state-level statutory compliance data for founders, CPAs, registered agents, and business owners. Unlike federal tax calculators that only estimate personal income and self-employment taxes, LLCTaxCheck calculates mandatory state maintenance fees owed directly to Secretaries of State and Departments of Revenue regardless of business profitability.

- 50-State Directory: https://llctaxcheck.com/states
- Multi-State Cost Benchmark: https://llctaxcheck.com/compare
- Statutory Rules Matrix: https://llctaxcheck.com/matrix

- Methodology & Statutory Citations: https://llctaxcheck.com/methodology

## Core Statutory Rules & Figures (Verified 2026/2027)

### High-Search Incorporation Jurisdictions:
- **California**: Mandatory minimum $800 annual franchise tax (FTB Form 3522) due April 15 for calendar year entities. Exemption applies only to first-year LLCs formed post-Jan 1, 2021. Additional graduated fee (FTB 3536) on gross receipts: $0 under $250k, $900 ($250k-$499k), $2,500 ($500k-$999k), $6,000 ($1M-$4.99M), $11,790 ($5M+). Biennial Statement of Information (LLC-12) fee: $20 ($250 late penalty). Statutory citation: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 17941, 17942.
- **Delaware**: Flat $400 annual franchise tax due June 1 (increased from $300 under House Bill 400). No annual corporate disclosure report required. Strict $200 non-negotiable statutory late penalty assessed on June 2 + 1.5% compounding monthly interest on the $600 delinquent balance. Statutory citation: 6 Del. C. § 18-1107 (as amended by HB 400).
- **Florida**: $138.75 annual report fee due May 1 via Sunbiz. Automatic non-waivable $400 late fee assessed on May 2 ($538.75 total). Administrative dissolution begins in September. Statutory citation: Fla. Stat. § 605.0213.
- **Texas**: $0 franchise tax for entities under the $2.47M no-tax-due threshold (Texas SB 3). Mandatory Public Information Report (PIR Form 05-102) due May 15. $50 late penalty + forfeiture of corporate privileges for missing PIR. Statutory citation: Tex. Tax Code § 171.203.
- **Wyoming**: Annual license tax due the 1st day of anniversary month. $60 flat minimum on assets up to $300,000; $0.0002 per dollar on assets exceeding $300,000 located within Wyoming. Statutory citation: Wyo. Stat. § 17-29-209.
- **Nevada**: $150 Annual List fee plus $200 State Business License fee ($350 total annual cost) due the last day of anniversary month. Late fee: $75 + $100 ($175 penalty). Statutory citation: NRS 76.100, NRS 86.263.
- **New York**: $9 biennial statement fee + annual pass-through entity filing fee (Form IT-204-LL) scaling from $25 to $4,500 based on NY gross income. Due March 15.
- **Massachusetts**: $500 annual report fee due on anniversary date of formation.
- **Tennessee**: $300 minimum annual report fee ($50/member, min $300, max $3,000) due April 15 + Franchise & Excise tax ($100 min).

### Zero-Fee States (No Mandatory Annual Maintenance Fee):
- **Arizona**: $0 annual report fee.
- **Idaho**: $0 annual report fee (annual report filing is mandatory, but fee is $0).
- **Missouri**: $0 annual report fee.
- **Ohio**: $0 annual report fee (Commercial Activity Tax / CAT applies only if gross receipts exceed $3M).
- **South Carolina**: $0 annual report fee.

### The "Foreign LLC Qualification" Tax Trap:
When founders incorporate in Delaware or Wyoming but conduct business, reside, or code from their home state (such as California or New York), they are legally transacting intrastate business (e.g., Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23101). They must foreign register and pay both the home state tax (e.g., $800 CA) and the incorporation state tax (e.g., $400 DE under HB 400), resulting in double maintenance costs.
